relevant_sign.before: Which of the following could be the slope field for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=x y?$
relevant_sign.after: Which of the following could be the slope field for the differential equation $\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=- x y?$

relevant_target.before_solution:
Notice that we are given an equation of the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}=f(x,y).
$$

The right-hand side is a function of $x$ and $y.$ This means that the slope field varies with both $x$ and $y.$

Of the given slope fields, we note the following slope field does not vary with $y$ given a fixed value of $x.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/generate/repairs/2026-10-20-early-cohort/jobs/17592186172040/review-1-policy-2-e0ceec0efc26ec01/assets/17592186172040/plots/d0647c9dc4664951ecefcc99ec18a9f3991a11630bb16746417fb2ec7855777d.png)

 

To see this more clearly, notice that if we draw a vertical line, the slopes do not vary.
